Subject: POC kickoff: Orbit staging access, session sequence & gating

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for agreeing to run a short POC with Redwood. We want to make the kickoff as practical as possible — hands-on prompt review, routing checks, and a small load/throughput smoke test so you can validate latency and cost on staging. To keep the session focused, below is a suggested sequence and the access items we need ahead of time.

Suggested 2-hour session sequence (we can compress if you prefer):
- 00:00–00:20: Introductions & mutual objectives (success criteria)
- 00:20–00:50: Staging endpoint walk-through + API key exchange
- 00:50–01:20: Prompt review & routing configuration (prompt templates + tool calling)
- 01:20–01:45: Short load test (burst of small requests + steady-state at expected TPS)
- 01:45–02:00: Next steps, security handoffs, and action items

Pre-kickoff checklist (please provide these 48 hours before the session):
- Sandbox/staging account emails for the attendees we should provision (list of emails)
- VPC allowlist IPs (or a list we can request from your network team)
- Any required KMS/HSM notes if keys are customer-managed
- Sample prompt set (5–10 prompts) you want us to run during the prompt review
- Expected peak concurrency and request/response size for the load test

Proposed kickoff windows (PT):
- Tue 2026-09-09 10:00–12:00
- Wed 2026-09-09 14:00–16:00

Attaching a short POC access guide and mutual action plan for your review. If those times don't work, let us know a couple of alternatives.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Looping in a quick engineering checklist from my side so the load test and routing checks are high signal: 
- Please confirm the average and 95th-percentile sequence lengths for the prompts you plan to test (we ask for this to pick appropriate KV cache sizing).
- For routing: do you want to validate model fallbacks (e.g., full-precision -> 8-bit quant variant) as part of the session? We can demonstrate automatic fallbacks on capacity pressure.
- If you'll run a 100-concurrent burst, state whether it's distributed across multiple clients or a single burst from one client — this impacts connection multiplexing behavior.

We have a short shared doc where you can paste the sample prompts and expected behaviors: https://redwood.app/s/drive/orbit-poc-plan (I'll pre-populate with an example prompt set).

—Grace O'Connor
Platform PM, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
